target.source: PyPI, both verified as LATEST via `pip index versions` before installing
target.selection_rationale: Chosen over alternatives per instructions to maximize architectural diversity: graph/node/edge execution model with a generic interrupt()/Command(resume=) primitive and pluggable checkpointer, structurally unlike both OpenAI Agents SDK's agent-loop+ToolApprovalItem model (EXP-003A) and Microsoft Agent Framework's Workflow+function_approval_request model (EXP-003B).

environment.model_dependence: None - every scenario uses plain deterministic Python graph node functions, no LLM/chat model in the loop. Unlike EXP-003A/B, LangGraph's low-level interrupt()/Command primitive does not require a model at all to exercise the authorization-relevant mechanics.

relevant_prior_evidence: labs/experiments/001-langgraph-approval-drift/ (this repo, pre-dates EXP-003C) - a real, already-confirmed finding against langchain==1.4.0's HumanInTheLoopMiddleware: approval bound to proposed arguments is not re-verified against executed arguments when a second, benign middleware reorders/mutates the call between approval and execution. Referenced, not repeated, per the operating rule not to redo closed work - see this report's H1 section for how it relates to (and is distinct from) what EXP-003C tests directly against raw langgraph.types.interrupt().
notes: API surface used (langgraph.types.interrupt/Command/Interrupt, langgraph.checkpoint.memory.InMemorySaver, langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite.SqliteSaver, langgraph.graph.StateGraph, langchain.agents.middleware.HumanInTheLoopMiddleware/InterruptOnConfig) confirmed by live introspection against the installed versions, not assumed from memory.
